title: kernel impact decomposition: regression hunt across flash/paged/continuous
body:
Overview:
This note documents an impact decomposition and regression-hunt for a set of runtime/kernel changes landed across late-2025 -> early-2026: flash-attention micro-optimizations, paged-KV activation, and a new continuous-batching scheduler. The goal: produce reproducible eval diffs across prompt sets used for onboarding open models and produce targeted mitigations.

Short summary of findings:
- Flash-attention v2 (opt kernels enabled) reduces median token latency by ~8-12% on short sequences but has a rare edge-case path that increases P99 latency on long-sequence multi-request workloads by up to 20% when combined with prefetch heuristics.
- Paged-KV enabled shows a quality regression on certain long-context prompt sets (dialogue-history stitching use-cases): exact-match/QA F1 drops of 1.2-3.5 percentage points for sequence lengths > 8k tokens. Root cause candidate: boundary-off-by-one during page-merge in the attention index leading to stale KV reads.
- Continuous-batching scheduler reduces aggregate cost and improves throughput for homogeneous small-request workloads (throughput +18% at 4–8 token medians) but increases latency variance (P95-P99 gap widened) and introduces request reordering in rare conditions which surfaced as hallucination/formatting inconsistencies in the streaming output for multi-turn evals.

Hypotheses we investigated:
1) Quality deltas on long-context prompt sets correlate with paged-KV page boundary handling; not flash-attention arithmetic changes.
2) P99 latency spikes occur when flash kernels attempt vectorized gather on partially-filled KV pages and fall back to a slower scalar path — fallback is not negligible.
3) Continuous-batching reordering plus aggressive prefix-caching may surface non-determinism in post-processing code paths (token-level detokenizer/serializer) rather than model weights.

Test matrix (what we ran):
- Model variants: open-model-A v1.2 pinned -> runtime v1.14 (baseline), runtime v1.15 (flash v2 enabled), runtime v1.16 (flash v2 + paged-KV), runtime v1.17 (flash v2 + paged-KV + continuous-batching)
- Prompt sets: onboarding_short_prompts (median 6 tokens), qna_long_history (median 3.6k tokens, tail > 9k), chat_multi_turn_stream (20–60 token turns with streaming enabled), code_completion_snippets (mixed lengths)
- Metrics collected: latency (p50/p90/p95/p99), tokens/sec, RMSE/Perplexity where applicable, QA-f1, exact-match (EM), BLEU/ROUGE for generation quality, deterministic-run delta (byte-level diff rate for canonical examples), and streaming-ordering errors per 1k requests.
- Environment: GPU A100 40GB baseline, same model weights, controlled noise (no other workloads), KV page size 128k tokens default, batch window 12ms for continuous scheduler.

Representative numeric diffs (summary table, deltas relative to runtime v1.14 baseline):
- onboarding_short_prompts (median 6 tokens):
  - median token latency: -10% (v1.15), -9% (v1.16), -11% (v1.17)
  - p99 latency: +2% (v1.15), +5% (v1.16), +12% (v1.17)
  - throughput (tokens/sec): +14% (v1.17)

- qna_long_history (median 3600 tokens, tail >9k):
  - QA F1: baseline 82.1% -> 80.9% (v1.16) -> 79.6% (v1.17); max drop observed 3.5 pts on engineered dialogue-stitch prompts
  - exact-match: 55.2% -> 53.9% (v1.16)
  - p99 latency: +18% (v1.16), +22% (v1.17)

- chat_multi_turn_stream (streaming enabled):
  - streaming ordering errors (per 1k): baseline 0.4 -> v1.17 3.1 (most concentrated in high concurrency runs)
  - detokenization byte-diff rate (canonical cases): 0.02% -> 0.18% v1.17

Investigation notes & reproduction traces:
- Repro step 1: run qna_long_history with deterministic seeds, paged-KV ON, reproduce EM drop on specific examples where the prompt contains repeated speaker markers (e.g., "User:" tokens repeated). Trace showed attention indices referencing page N when expected page N-1 for tokens right at the page boundary.
- Repro step 2: enable flash-attention fallback logs (low-level tracing). On P99 spike traces, we observed fallback to scalar gather for ~0.6% of tokens during page-merge windows; each fallback adds ~0.8–1.2ms per token incrementally.
- Repro step 3: continuous-batching instrumentation showed occasional request reordering when scheduler preempted an in-flight batch to preserve latency SLOs; streamed chunks from re-ordered requests were interleaved in the serializer queue for ~0.15% of sessions, causing malformed JSON streaming chunks for downstream parsers.

Root cause hypotheses and confidence levels:
- Paged-KV page-merge boundary bug (high confidence): index arithmetic (off-by-one) when merging tail of page A into head of page B. Repro steps and unit tests reproduce on a minimal harness.
- Flash fallback cost (medium confidence): fallback path exists and is slower; combined with page-merge it happens more often. Review of kernel commit shows optimistic vector path assumes page alignment that does not hold after the page-merge sequence.
- Continuous-batching reordering (medium confidence): scheduler preemption logic does not update serialization ordering metadata reliably under high concurrency; secondary issue in serializer queue ordering.

Immediate mitigations applied to staging cluster (notes):
- Rollback paged-KV ON for affected customers and gating by config flag: paged_kv=experimental -> paged_kv=off by default until fix. (status: applied 2026-02-05)
- Added a fast assertion & unit test to page-merge code to catch off-by-one and added a small integration test in CI. (status: PR open: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/604)
- For flash-attention fallback: instrumented and added a metric to count scalar-fallback events; disabled the aggressive prefetch for KV pages until we confirm alignment guarantees. (status: metric live, prefetch disabled 2026-02-20)
- For continuous-batching: switched to conservative non-preemptive mode for streaming-enabled routes and added a serialization barrier to ensure ordering for any streaming session. (status: staged)

Recommendations & next steps:
- Patch paged-KV merge logic (high priority). Proposed patch: enforce inclusive-exclusive indexing semantics in page copy routines, add fuzz tests with random boundary offsets. Owner: Liam Chen. Target: patch + canary by 2026-03-12.
- Add kernel-level alignment sanity checks before vectorized gathers; if misaligned, attempt small memmove to align rather than taking scalar fallback when possible (reduces fallback cost). Owner: Sofia Martinez. Target: RFC by 2026-03-01.
- For continuous-batching, make ordering guarantees explicit for streaming routes: new config per-route 'streaming_ordering: strict|best_effort' with default strict for now. Owner: Benjy Kapoor. Target: rollout by 2026-03-05.
- Expand onboarding evals to include a focused long-context regression suite (100 curated prompts that hit page boundaries) and add a nightly regression job comparing EM/QA-F1 to baseline with alerting on >1 point drop.

Open questions / edge cases to investigate:
- Does a different KV page size (64k vs 128k) change the frequency of the off-by-one bug? Early experiments suggest smaller page sizes reduce incidence but do not eliminate it.
- Are there specific tokenizers/byte-level encodings that exacerbate the page boundary alignment problem? We should run the 3 most common tokenizers used by customers on the long-context suite.
- How will these mitigations interact with Dedicated/Private deployments where customers may enable experimental features? Need coordinated rollout notes and feature flags.

Action items (owners + rough ETA):
- Fix paged-KV index arithmetic + CI tests (Liam Chen) - ETA 2026-03-10
- Kernel alignment RFC and micro-patch to avoid scalar fallback (Sofia Martinez) - ETA 2026-03-12
- Scheduler ordering guard for streaming routes & config flag (Benjy Kapoor) - ETA 2026-03-08
- Nightly regression job with long-context set + alerting (Asha Patel) - ETA 2026-03-03
- Customer communication draft for Dedicated customers currently using paged-KV (Product/CS) - draft by 2026-02-28

Appendix: sample failing examples (anonymized)
- Example A (qna_long_history): repeated "User:" tokens every ~4096 tokens. EM baseline 0 -> failing runtime shows answer missing last constraint (trace points to KV index referencing page+1).
- Example B (chat_multi_turn_stream): high-concurrency run with streaming ordering error; partial JSON chunk arrives, then later the chunk for previous request interleaves; downstream JSON parser throws and client sees truncated assistant output.

Notes on data & reproducibility:
- All eval runs and raw traces are saved under s3://redwood-evals/2026-02-pagedkv-regression/ with experiment manifest in the linked_artifacts above. Jobs are deterministic given the seed parameter; reproduction scripts are in runtime/tools/regression/reproduce.sh (linked in PR).

If you are triaging a customer report that looks like this, immediate triage checklist:
1) Check whether customer route has paged-KV enabled; if yes, flip experimental flag and re-run sample failing prompt to confirm improvement.
2) If streaming ordering problems: move route to conservative batching mode and report job id to eng-oncall.
3) Collect trace ids, attach to JIRA-APPL-842, and ping SLA-support for high-severity incidents.

End of note.
